findings.description: publicly_accessible = true exposes the MySQL instance to the internet, so the database endpoint and port 3306 can be reached from any network, and combined with the weak static 'admin' username and hardcoded password this materially raises the risk of brute-force and direct exploitation.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the database storage, snapshots, and read replicas unencrypted, so anyone with access to the underlying volumes or backups can read all catalog data in plaintext.

The EC2 user_data script writes the database password (var.password) in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc, which is served by an Apache docroot and is retrievable from instance metadata and the EC2 console/API by anyone with read access, leaking the DB credential.

The database password is passed as a plaintext variable/literal (password = var.password) instead of being sourced from a secrets manager, and 'ignore_changes = ["password"]' prevents rotation; combined with username 'admin' the credential is guessable and long-lived.

The ingress rule opens TCP/3306 to the entire VPC CIDR rather than a specific application security group, so any instance or workload in the VPC (including compromised or unrelated hosts) can reach the database on the MySQL port.

The catalog app role is granted s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource '*', giving the EC2 instance full control of storage, compute, and databases across the account; compromise of the instance yields broad account takeover capability.

An egress rule allowing protocol '-1' from port 0 to port 0 on 0.0.0.0/0 permits the security group members to initiate outbound connections anywhere, facilitating data exfiltration and command-and-control traffic from compromised instances.

The generated PHP page reads $_POST['NAME'] and $_POST['ADDRESS'] directly without server-side validation, and the values are interpolated into HTML output; this creates reflected/XSS and injection surface in a page that is publicly reachable via the instance's public DNS.

backup_retention_period = 0 and monitoring_interval = 0 disable automated backups and enhanced monitoring, reducing the ability to detect and recover from data tampering or exfiltration against the publicly exposed database.
